The defect is verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: The server handler never enforces uniqueness within the `guests` array itself — the uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog's Zod schema, while the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) is just z.array(z.string().email()). Any non-UI caller (API client, script) sends guests: ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] and two identical attendee rows are created for the booking, both receiving calendar REQUEST emails, with no way to deduplicate later through this API.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.schema.ts`, the server accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones, but does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. It then does `attendees.createMany` with `guestsFullDetails`, so duplicate entries in `guests` can result in duplicate create attempts (either inserting duplicates if allowed, or triggering a DB error if constrained). The client-side dialog adds a uniqueness refine, but non-UI callers can bypass it, so the finding about missing server-side uniqueness enforcement is grounded in the diff.
